correctness.rationale: Direct reconstruction: the full graph automorphism group is simultaneous S_n and side swap; proper colors shared across both sides occur only as distinct matched diagonal pairs, so a proper coloring is distinguishing exactly when its ordered pairs are distinct and at least one nondiagonal. The finite injection count U follows from the principle of inclusion--exclusion over omitted rows/columns; unique decomposition by shared colors and exclusive palettes proves the polynomial formula. Optimal mixed-color threshold follows from n<=t+floor((k-t)^2/4), the known sharp minimum k, and integer capacity comparison; equality forces t=1 and ab=n-1. Direct brute force applies every automorphism for all q<=5 at n=3,4 and separately verifies n<=23 thresholds.

Full-text comparison with Laflamme--Seyffarth (2009), section 2, establishes that the source proves the minimum color number and uses ordered pairs but does not state the full q-coloring enumeration or exact shared-color refinement and mixed-optimal count. Novelty risk of differently indexed earlier enumeration remains.

value.rationale: Beyond the previously established minimum number of colors, the result enumerates all properly symmetry-breaking labeled palettes for a natural highly symmetric bipartite family. The full distribution by cross-side color sharing detects an unexpected phenomenon at precisely the first order of each palette-size threshold; it gives explicit numbers of those exceptional optimal colorings (e.g. 3600 at n=5 and 604800 at n=7). This is a natural exact enumerative invariant and not a renamed earlier bound, arbitrary slice, or known table reproduction.
